[Interview, 2016-01-16, All Things Considered]
HOST: Interesting. GUEST, you are a fan, right, 'cause you actually went down to help out on her first...
GUEST: Yes.

HOST: ...Campaign for governor. She's since been reelected. Tell us about - how is this sitting with you? Did you - were you aware of this, by the way, all this hubbub around...
GUEST: Well, very much. In fact, being in politics, you always watch what's going on. But I think - let's take to it - I think the core group - the fundamental of the Republican Party - she identified and defined that. She tells her story. At the same time, she also says look, we're going through trying times, which we are. And the last seven years, which she pointed out in her speech, has been very tough on middle Americans, a lot of hard-working frustrated Americans who cannot really find a way to get back to good times. And we've gone through home financial crisis, families have broken apart. It's been challenging times. And what she was trying to portray and share is a softer side of the Republican Party, which we've never been able to message very - in a - articulate it in an effective way. I think she did a phenomenal job. And yes, we have the right to speak what our minds, say, and it didn't sit with well with certain people. Well, that's fine; but the good thing is she was being inclusive and together. And if you see her remarks after that, she said no, I just want to basically be an inclusive party. And that's what she was trying to get out.

HOST: What do you make of the blowback though?
GUEST: Look, she's taken some solid actions in the South - brought businesses back and then took down the flag. She's done some positive things, and that's a reason why Reince Priebus, the RNC chairman, and Mitch McConnell both felt that she is the new face and the new messenger of the Republican Party.

HOST: But the question is...

HOST: Go ahead, Sam.

HOST: ...Does the base want to see that face?
GUEST: Well...

HOST: The base of the party in this election is very angry, and she's trying to present a face that is not that angry.

HOST: Let me get Ravi in here. Ravi, do you a dog in this fight? Go ahead.

HOST: Yeah, she is. Yeah.

HOST: Well, yeah.

HOST: (Laughter) I mean, well, yeah. Go ahead, Ravi.

HOST: I think that remains to be seen.

HOST: But Ravi, let me ask you this. The whole - the other side of it that Sam highlighted, which is some people saying, you know, you Anglicized your name - you know, so what do you make of that?

HOST: Yeah. And here's the thing, people of all races from all over the place get nicknames. You know, I mean, like, nicknames happen. We should - like, we can't always...

HOST: ...Assume because someone takes on a nickname that it is for these bigger, larger reasons.

HOST: GUEST, go ahead.
GUEST: ...When I came here, in fact, a lot of people wanted me to change my name. And of course, if you - my name GUEST - God, it's a singsong name...

HOST: Workshopping (laughter).
GUEST: I didn't choose to change my name because I felt like people who know me for who I am and how I am. The fact is, you know, it all depends on how people want to fit in. And I think as we are a country of liberty and your choice, it's up to you what you decide to do in the end.

HOST: And we do have a president who's named Barack.
GUEST: Yeah, exactly.

HOST: Sure, you can say that. But yeah - yeah, I like Jennifer Lawrence, but I - well, anyway - all right, I'm going to give GUEST the last word. Do you care? Do you follow this stuff? You're the civilian here.
GUEST: I don't want to make more about this. I think it is what it is, and I think - I love "The Martian." I loved Leonardo's role, and...

HOST: You're not confusing Matt Damon and Leonardo DiCaprio, are you?
GUEST: No, I'm not.

HOST: OK, I'm just making sure that we weren't having a little reverse...

HOST: Are you saying they all look alike, Michel?

HOST: I was not. I'm just making sure that...

[Interview, 2017-01-14, All Things Considered]
HOST: Both of you are.

HOST: GUEST, thoughts?
GUEST: Well, I think he put him in his place. If you are fake news, this president is going to get back to you.

HOST: Who's covering - who's reporting fake news?

HOST: Who is reporting fake news?
GUEST: They reported which was not true...

HOST: First of all, it's an oxymoron. If it's fake, by definition it's not news. So let me just put a stake in that if we could.
GUEST: But anyway...

HOST: But go ahead.
GUEST: He will basically give you straight talk. And he's looking for a more fair and balanced and straight talk in terms of the news.

HOST: What did CNN report that was inaccurate?
GUEST: Well, CNN reported about that - the...

HOST: They did not report these salacious details. That was another news organization.
GUEST: But they still...

HOST: They reported the fact that the president and the president-elect were briefed about this dossier that existed. You don't think that's important?
GUEST: Well, according to Trump, it is not. It is basically - what he came out and said is that it's not true, and I'm not going to really give you the respect and time to answer your question because you're not reporting correctly.

HOST: You still haven't told me what he said that was inaccurate - what CNN reported that was inaccurate.
GUEST: CNN reported the information that was - basically came out from the intelligence agency or some part and which is not true.

HOST: A former British intelligence officer who was reporting this for opposition research within the Republican Party, but they did not report these salacious details. That was another news organization. That's just...
GUEST: But they highlighted the story.

HOST: ...That is a fact. That is not fake news. That is news. It is accurate.

HOST: OK.
